ticket.title: Ticket file store with atomic writes, per-ticket locking and timestamp-ordered replay
ticket.description:
New store layout: .gaugeblock/storypole/tickets/KEY.json holding ticket (TaskNode), events (ordered LedgerEvents) and external (optional tracker mapping). Writers write a temp file and rename, which is atomic within one filesystem, and take a per-ticket advisory lock, because storypole-core has no write atomicity or locking at all today (no flock, no rename), so the CLI and the daemon can clobber one ticket. Replay inside a file orders by (timestamp_ms, event uuid) rather than by file position: file order is how a union-merged ledger lets a stale status win. The append-only path is retired behind the migration flag in SP-35.

PROGRESS 2026-11-08 (first slice, branch feat/gb-329-ticket-file-store, commit af7baff):

The record store exists and is tested: tickets/<KEY>.json holds the task, ordered events and an optional
external mapping; writes are temp-file-plus-rename; reads refuse a key that could escape the directory;
replay orders by the event's own clock and id. Five tests green, 97 storypole-core tests green, clippy
clean, every file under the 250-line limit.

MEASURED (darwin, warm build, same machine, sequential): with the per-ticket lock bypassed the
concurrency test reports 8 of 41 events surviving - 33 silently lost to a read-modify-write race. With
the lock, 41 of 41. The ledger had this safety for free through one O_APPEND write per event; a
whole-file record does not, which is why the lock was the first thing built rather than an addition.

STILL OWED before this ticket can be verified: StorypoleStore does not read the record yet (it still
opens ledger.jsonl), and the two-worktree gate in the acceptance criteria has not been written - a
test that adds a real git worktree, runs two agents against it concurrently, and asserts no lost update
plus lease visibility. Second slice.

PROGRESS 2026-11-08, second slice (commit 04d0f5e, branch feat/gb-329-ticket-file-store):

The store now has an explicit storage mode. A repository with a tickets directory reads and writes records;
one without keeps the ledger. Exactly one is authoritative, because dual-writing is the divergence GB-79
documents. Mode is detected from the directory, so ls explains the behaviour. The records index mirrors the
ledger index: disposable projection, staleness from a directory fingerprint.

TWO-WORKTREE GATE, half satisfied and measured: both worktrees of one repository resolve to the same
.gaugeblock (asserted), and two agents appending from two checkouts keep all 21 events. The remaining half
is honesty about method: the test injects events through tickets::append_event rather than driving two real
clients, because no CLI verb writes a record until this wiring lands in the handlers. Cross-worktree lease
visibility is SP-39, not this ticket.

A rule the store needed: a ticket's first event creates its file, and every later event must find one. Found
by the first test run - the creation failed with 'No such file or directory' because the record it was meant
to create did not exist yet - and the fix had to refuse the looser alternative, where a status change on a
missing ticket invents a record from nothing.
The tickets directory was also created after init in the test helper, so init had chosen the legacy
.storypole path and the reopened store resolved somewhere else. Both were test-side, both were caught only
by running.

Deliberately still InProgress: the handlers do not drive records yet, so SP-36 and SP-37 remain blocked on
wiring rather than on design.

CORRECTION 2026-11-08, probe with the installed binary in a fresh repository:

  mkdir -p .gaugeblock/storypole/tickets
  storypole add 'a records-mode task' --kind docs   -> Created CO-1 [Docs]
  storypole claim CO-1 cline-agent                  -> InProgress
  storypole update CO-1 --priority 1                -> P1

  tickets/CO-1.json events: task_created, task_claimed, status_changed, task_updated
  ledger.jsonl: 0 bytes
  storypole list: CO-1 docs P1 InProgress

This makes the caveat recorded in the previous slice WRONG. It said the handlers do not drive records and
that SP-36/SP-37 were blocked on wiring. They are not: every handler goes through record_event, which
routes on the storage mode, so records mode became reachable the moment the directory existed. What is
missing is not wiring but the migration that creates the directory, which is SP-37.

The claim and update paths are the interesting ones, because they carry no task: their owner is resolved
from the index, which is the code path a naive implementation gets wrong.

Still owed for this ticket: the two-worktree test drives tickets::append_event rather than two real clients,
and that is now cheap to fix - the probe above is exactly what a two-client test would do, from two
checkouts. Cross-worktree lease visibility stays with SP-39.

SLICE 3 2026-11-08 (commit 830b9cc): the two-client test exists and it found two defects, so this ticket is
now blocked by them rather than by design.

The test builds a repository, adds a linked worktree, and drives the built binary from both checkouts at
once. Both cases are committed IGNORED, with the reason naming the ticket, because a failing test cannot be
committed as an expected result and deleting the reproduction would discard the expensive part.

SP-44: two concurrent adds mint the same key and the second record overwrites the first. Observed: two
parallel adds produced exactly one file, so a ticket was silently lost. The per-ticket lock cannot help -
the writers never touch the same path until the overwrite, and the key is chosen before the file exists.

SP-45: the store cannot be found from a linked worktree. Resolution walks ancestors and a worktree is a
sibling directory, so GaugeblockPaths::discover (which resolves through the git common dir, exactly as ADR
0001 says) is never consulted. Observed: four of eight concurrent updates returned Task not found for a
ticket that exists - the four that ran from the worktree.

SP-45 also corrects this ticket's own claim. The worktree test downstream proved that BOTH checkouts
resolve to one .gaugeblock, and that is true of GaugeblockPaths; it is not true of the store, which uses a
different resolver. Until SP-45 is fixed, no ticket layout makes two agents in two worktrees share state.

VERIFIED AND MERGED 2026-11-08. Receipt: branch feat/gb-347-shared-keys, 15 commits, chain storypole, exit 0.

The gate is now the two-client test, rewritten for the state that exists rather than the state it once assumed:

  a_ticket_created_in_each_checkout_gets_its_own_file_and_its_own_number
      records follow the branch (CO-1 committed, worktree adds CO-2) and numbers come from the shared counter,
      so two branches cannot mint one key (SP-46).
  a_lease_taken_in_one_checkout_blocks_the_other
      the ticket is visible in both checkouts because it was committed; the lease is visible in both because it
      lives in the git directory. The refusal says 'another checkout' (SP-39).

Both pass without ignores. The five stacked branches are merged into storypole main (74451b3) after a full gate
run on the merge result: clippy clean, 138 tests, audits pass. Nine commits spot-checked as ancestors of main.

What changed since this ticket was filed: it was Blocked on SP-45 and SP-39, both of which turned out to be
one decision - which state a command sees - now recorded as ADR 0009.
acceptance_criteria: the two-worktree concurrency test fails against the append-only implementation and passes after; a killed writer leaves the old file or the new one, never a truncated one; replay of a file whose lines are shuffled yields identical state

The test builds a repository, adds a linked worktree, and drives the built binary from both checkouts at

SP-44: two concurrent adds mint the same key and the second record overwrites the first. Observed: two
parallel adds produced exactly one file, so a ticket was silently lost. The per-ticket lock cannot help -
the writers never touch the same path until the overwrite, and the key is chosen before the file exists.

SP-45: the store cannot be found from a linked worktree. Resolution walks ancestors and a worktree is a
sibling directory, so GaugeblockPaths::discover (which resolves through the git common dir, exactly as ADR
0001 says) is never consulted. Observed: four of eight concurrent updates returned Task not found for a
ticket that exists - the four that ran from the worktree.

SP-45 also corrects this ticket's own claim. The worktree test downstream proved that BOTH checkouts
resolve to one .gaugeblock, and that is true of GaugeblockPaths; it is not true of the store, which uses a
different resolver. Until SP-45 is fixed, no ticket layout makes two agents in two worktrees share state.
